result.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService updateEvent, the diff changes the fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. But that branch is only reached when externalCalendarId is falsy (the ternary condition), so find() never matches and selectedCalendar is always undefined — previously it fell back to the event's own destinationCalendar.externalId. Same dead logic in deleteEvent. This is a real regression verifiable directly from the diff lines.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()`, the fallback logic for `selectedCalendar` was changed from `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), this now searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `undefined`/`null`), which will typically return `undefined` instead of using the event’s destination calendar. This matches the finding: the previous behavior used the event's destination calendar, the new code commonly yields `undefined`.
